h1: Couples Retreats in Alaska: What Happens, What It Costs, and Whether It Is Worth It
sub: When weekly counseling feels too slow, a retreat gives your relationship focused, uninterrupted time to break through. Here is exactly how it works.
bodyHtml:
Home / Services / Couples Retreats in Alaska: What Happens, What It Costs, and Whether It Is Worth It

PHOTO PLACEHOLDER, add a warm, on-brand image for this page

If weekly counseling feels too slow for what your relationship is facing, a couples retreat may be exactly what you need. A retreat gives you focused, uninterrupted time to get past the surface fight and reach the thing underneath, guided the whole way. Here are honest answers to the questions couples ask most before booking one.

What happens during a couples retreat?

Instead of fifty minutes once a week, a retreat gives you concentrated time over several days to work through what is really going on, with your counselor guiding you the entire way. There is room to slow down, get past the argument you always have, and practice a new way of being together before the time is up. Couples leave having actually done the work, not just talked about it.

Is a couples retreat worth it?

For the right situation, yes. Weekly sessions can stall when each one gets reset by the next crisis before progress takes hold. A retreat removes those interruptions and lets change build on itself. It is especially worth it when a relationship is in real crisis, when trust has been broken, or when distance and busy schedules make consistent weekly sessions hard, which is common across Alaska.

Can a retreat save a marriage?

A retreat cannot do the work for you, but it can be the thing that finally gets a stuck couple unstuck. Many couples find that concentrated time, in a safe and guided space, breaks a pattern that years of weekly attempts could not. It is often the turning point, followed by lighter ongoing work.

The 3-day and the 5-day retreat

Our 3-day retreat is the standard for most couples, enough time to reconnect, break a recurring pattern, or strengthen a solid relationship. Our 5-day retreat is designed for couples recovering from a crisis or a breach of trust, such as an affair, where rebuilding trust needs more time. You can read a full comparison in 3-day vs 5-day couples retreat, and how retreats compare to weekly work in intensive or weekly.

What does a couples retreat cost?

Retreat pricing depends on the length and format that fit your situation, and it is private pay. We are always happy to talk openly about cost and help you choose the option that genuinely fits, never the longer one just because it is longer. Reach out and we will walk you through it.

What to expect at your first session

Reaching out is the hardest step, so we keep the first one simple. Your first session is an unhurried conversation to understand what brought you in and what you are hoping for. There is no pressure to tell your whole story at once. It is also your chance to see whether we are the right fit, because the relationship between you and your counselor matters more than anything else. Sessions run about fifty minutes, in person or by secure video, and we will explain confidentiality and next steps clearly. You can read more in what to expect in your first therapy session.

Common questions

What happens during a couples retreat?

You spend focused, guided time over several days working through what is really going on, with room to get past the surface argument and practice new patterns. Couples leave having done the work, not just discussed it.

Is a marriage retreat worth the cost?

For couples in crisis, or those stuck in patterns weekly sessions cannot touch, it often is. A retreat removes the weekly reset and lets change build on itself, which frequently becomes the turning point.

Should we choose the 3-day or 5-day retreat?

The 3-day retreat suits most couples reconnecting or strengthening a solid relationship. The 5-day is designed for recovery from a crisis or a breach of trust like an affair, where rebuilding trust needs more time. We will help you decide.

bodyHtml:
Home / Services / Couples and Marriage Counseling in Wasilla, Alaska

PHOTO PLACEHOLDER, add a warm, on-brand image for this page

If your relationship has drifted into distance, conflict, or the same fight on repeat, you are not alone, and it is not too late. At SoundHeart Counseling in the Mat-Su Valley, we help Wasilla couples move from disconnection back to closeness, whether you are facing a specific crisis or a slow drift you cannot quite name.

Help for real Wasilla couples

Couples come to us at every stage, some in acute crisis, some simply wanting to feel like partners again. We work with communication that has broken down, trust that has been shaken, intimacy that has faded, and the recurring conflicts that wear a relationship thin. Wherever you are, the goal is the same, to help you understand the cycle you are stuck in and build something safer and more connected.

What we help couples with

  • Constant conflict and the same fight that never resolves.
  • Feeling like roommates, with the spark faded.
  • Recovering after an affair or a breach of trust.
  • Deciding whether to stay, through discernment counseling.
  • Preparing for marriage with premarital counseling.

A different kind of couples work

Our approach, the NeuroRelational Belonging model, is built on a simple idea. Connection is not a personality trait you either have or lack. It is a set of patterns your nervous system learned, and anything learned can be practiced into something new. Rather than only talking about your problems, we help you and your partner practice safety and repair until connection feels natural again. Learn more about how and why couples therapy works.

In person or by telehealth

We see Wasilla and Mat-Su couples in person, and we offer secure telehealth for couples anywhere in Alaska, which helps when schedules, weather, or distance make weekly visits hard. For couples in deeper crisis, we also offer immersive couples retreats that concentrate real change into a focused block of time.

What to expect at your first session

Reaching out is the hardest step, so we keep the first one simple. Your first session is an unhurried conversation to understand what brought you in and what you are hoping for. There is no pressure to tell your whole story at once. It is also your chance to see whether we are the right fit, because the relationship between you and your counselor matters more than anything else. Sessions run about fifty minutes, in person or by secure video, and we will explain confidentiality and next steps clearly. You can read more in what to expect in your first therapy session.

Common questions

Does couples counseling actually work?

Yes. Research shows most couples who engage in therapy improve, and outcomes are strongest when couples come before resentment has fully set in. Good couples work helps you understand your cycle, calm reactive patterns, and rebuild safety and closeness.

Can we come if only one of us is sure about it?

Yes. Even one motivated partner can shift a relationship, and we often work with couples where one person is hesitant. If you are genuinely unsure whether to stay together, discernment counseling is designed for that.

Do you offer couples counseling in Wasilla in person?

Yes. We see couples in person in the Mat-Su Valley and also offer secure telehealth across Alaska, so distance or a busy schedule does not have to keep you from getting help.

h1: EMDR and Trauma Therapy in Wasilla and the Mat-Su Valley
sub: If the past still runs the present, healing is possible. We offer EMDR and trauma informed therapy for Wasilla and Mat-Su clients, in person or by telehealth.
bodyHtml:
Home / Services / EMDR and Trauma Therapy in Wasilla and the Mat-Su Valley

PHOTO PLACEHOLDER, add a warm, on-brand image for this page

If something you lived through still shows up in your sleep, your relationships, or your body's alarm going off when you are safe, you are not broken and you are not stuck for good. At SoundHeart Counseling in the Mat-Su Valley, we offer EMDR and trauma informed therapy that helps your brain finally process what it could not at the time.

Trauma is treatable

Trauma is one of the most treatable conditions in mental health, and yet so many people carry it for years thinking that is just how they are. Whether your trauma came from a single event or from years of difficult experiences, we help Wasilla and Mat-Su clients move from surviving to genuinely healing.

What we help with

  • PTSD and the alarm system that will not switch off.
  • The adult effects of childhood trauma, including anxiety and people pleasing.
  • Recovery after emotional abuse and toxic relationships.
  • Trauma carried by first responders and those whose work follows them home.

What is EMDR?

EMDR is a structured, well researched therapy that helps the brain reprocess stuck memories so they stop feeling like they are happening now. You do not have to retell every detail, and the work is paced to feel manageable. Many people find significant relief, sometimes quickly. Learn more in what is EMDR and does it really work, and about the hope on the other side in post-traumatic growth.

In person in the Valley, or by telehealth

We offer trauma therapy in person for Wasilla and Palmer clients, and by secure telehealth across Alaska. Because healing happens best in safety, we go at your pace, building steadiness first.

What to expect at your first session

Reaching out is the hardest step, so we keep the first one simple. Your first session is an unhurried conversation to understand what brought you in and what you are hoping for. There is no pressure to tell your whole story at once. It is also your chance to see whether we are the right fit, because the relationship between you and your counselor matters more than anything else. Sessions run about fifty minutes, in person or by secure video, and we will explain confidentiality and next steps clearly. You can read more in what to expect in your first therapy session.

Common questions

Do I have to talk about my trauma in detail for EMDR?

No. EMDR does not require retelling the trauma in depth. The focus is on how the memory is stored, and early sessions center on building safety and trust before any processing begins.

How many EMDR sessions will I need?

It depends on your history. A single event trauma can sometimes resolve in a handful of sessions, while complex or repeated trauma takes longer. We tailor the pace to you.

Can EMDR help complex or repeated trauma?

Yes. While it usually takes longer than for a single event, EMDR is effective for complex trauma built up over years. We build safety and stability first, then process at a pace that works for you.

h1: Counseling for First Responders and Veterans in Alaska
sub: You carry what others never see. We offer confidential, trauma informed care for Alaska's first responders, veterans, and the families who stand beside them.
bodyHtml:
Home / Services / Counseling for First Responders and Veterans in Alaska

PHOTO PLACEHOLDER, add a warm, on-brand image for this page

Police, firefighters, EMS, dispatchers, corrections officers, child welfare workers, and veterans carry things most people never have to see. When the job starts following you home, in your sleep, your temper, or your sudden reactions, that is not weakness. It is what trauma does, and it is treatable. We offer confidential, trauma informed care for Alaska's first responders and veterans.

The weight of the work

It is rarely one call or one deployment. It is the accumulation, scene after scene, tour after tour, inside a culture that often prizes toughness and silence. That combination is why first responders and veterans carry higher rates of trauma, depression, and burnout, and why a smell, a sound, or a certain light can bring it all back. Read more in when the job follows you home.

What we help with

  • PTSD and the alarm system that will not switch off.
  • Secondary and vicarious trauma, especially for those exposed to others' suffering, including child welfare workers.
  • Moral injury, the deep wound of choices that violated your own values.
  • Anger, numbness, sleep problems, and the strain on relationships at home.

Confidential and effective

Getting help does not mean you are broken or unfit for the work. It means you are human and have carried more than anyone should carry alone. EMDR is highly effective for the way traumatic memories get stuck, and it is widely used with first responders and veterans. Healing does not stop at symptom relief either. Many find real growth and meaning on the other side.

For the families too

The job affects the whole household. We also support partners and families navigating deployment, reintegration, and the strain of loving someone who carries so much. If you are ever in crisis, call or text 988.

What to expect at your first session

Reaching out is the hardest step, so we keep the first one simple. Your first session is an unhurried conversation to understand what brought you in and what you are hoping for. There is no pressure to tell your whole story at once. It is also your chance to see whether we are the right fit, because the relationship between you and your counselor matters more than anything else. Sessions run about fifty minutes, in person or by secure video, and we will explain confidentiality and next steps clearly. You can read more in what to expect in your first therapy session.

Common questions

Is counseling for first responders confidential?

Yes. We provide confidential, trauma informed care. Seeking help does not mean you are unfit for the work, and what you share stays between us within the usual professional and legal protections.

Why do certain smells or sounds trigger me?

During a traumatic event, the brain records the surrounding sensory details along with the danger. Later, a similar smell, sound, or light can trigger the full stress response as if it were happening again. This is a hallmark of PTSD and is treatable.

What is moral injury?

Moral injury is a deep wound to your conscience that occurs when the job forces choices that violate your own values. It is common among first responders and veterans and deserves real care, alongside any trauma symptoms.

Counseling for Palmer couples at every stage

Both are worth showing up for. We help with the full range of what couples face, from recurring conflict and lost intimacy to rebuilding after a serious breach of trust.

What we help couples with

  • Communication breakdowns and the patterns that predict trouble.
  • One partner who shuts down or withdraws during conflict.

  • Reconnecting as empty nesters or after years of putting the kids first.
  • Money conflict, and what it is really about.

Practice, not just talk

Our NeuroRelational approach helps couples do more than analyze their problems. You practice new ways of connecting until your nervous systems learn that closeness is safe again. When a relationship needs more than a weekly hour, an intensive or a couples retreat can help you break through faster.

Convenient for the Valley

Palmer sits at the heart of the Mat-Su Valley, and we serve it both in person and by secure telehealth. If getting to weekly appointments is hard, telehealth lets you do the work from home, on your schedule.

What to expect at your first session

Reaching out is the hardest step, so we keep the first one simple. Your first session is an unhurried conversation to understand what brought you in and what you are hoping for. There is no pressure to tell your whole story at once. It is also your chance to see whether we are the right fit, because the relationship between you and your counselor matters more than anything else. Sessions run about fifty minutes, in person or by secure video, and we will explain confidentiality and next steps clearly. You can read more in what to expect in your first therapy session.

Common questions

How long does marriage counseling take?

It depends on your goals. Focused concerns can improve in a few sessions, while rebuilding after a deeper wound like an affair takes longer. We will give you a realistic sense early on, and an intensive or retreat can speed things up.

What if my spouse refuses to come?

It is still worth reaching out. Individual work can shift a relationship, and we can help you communicate in ways that make your partner more likely to join later. If you are unsure whether to stay, discernment counseling is built for that.

What if we have tried counseling before and it did not help?

That is common, and it does not mean your relationship cannot change. Sometimes the fit or the approach was not right. Our work focuses on practicing new patterns, not just talking, and an intensive can help you break through.

h1: Online Therapy and Telehealth Across Alaska
sub: For a state this big, telehealth can be a lifeline. Get effective, private counseling from wherever you are in Alaska.
bodyHtml:
Home / Services / Online Therapy and Telehealth Across Alaska

PHOTO PLACEHOLDER, add a warm, on-brand image for this page

For a state as vast as Alaska, this is one of the most useful things to know. Online therapy is as effective as in person care for most concerns, and it removes the exact barriers, distance, weather, and provider shortages, that keep so many Alaskans from getting help. Wherever you are in the state, support can reach you.

Does online therapy actually work?

Yes. A large body of research shows telehealth produces outcomes comparable to in person therapy for most people and concerns, including anxiety, depression, trauma, and relationship issues. The working relationship that drives change forms just as well over a good video connection. You can read more in does online therapy actually work.

Why it matters so much in Alaska

  • No long drive on icy roads to reach a counselor.
  • Access for rural and remote communities far from any provider.
  • Continuity through moves, deployments, seasonal work, and hard winters.
  • More choice, since you are not limited to therapists in your own town.

Who we help by telehealth

We offer secure telehealth for individuals, couples, and families across Alaska, covering everything from anxiety and depression to trauma, couples work, and seasonal depression. If you have wondered whether where you live means going without support, it does not have to.

Getting the most from it

Find a private, quiet space, use headphones for sound and privacy, and log on a few minutes early. Our guide on what to expect in your first session walks you through the rest.

What to expect at your first session

Reaching out is the hardest step, so we keep the first one simple. Your first session is an unhurried conversation to understand what brought you in and what you are hoping for. There is no pressure to tell your whole story at once. It is also your chance to see whether we are the right fit, because the relationship between you and your counselor matters more than anything else. Sessions run about fifty minutes, in person or by secure video, and we will explain confidentiality and next steps clearly. You can read more in what to expect in your first therapy session.

Common questions

Is online therapy as effective as in person?

For most common concerns, yes. Research shows telehealth produces outcomes comparable to in person care, and the therapeutic relationship forms well over a good video connection.

Can I get therapy in rural Alaska?

Yes. Telehealth lets you work with a licensed Alaska therapist from anywhere in the state, including remote communities, often much sooner than waiting for a local opening.

Is telehealth private and secure?

We use a secure, private platform for telehealth. For the most privacy, join from a quiet space where you will not be overheard, using headphones if you can.

h1: Postpartum Depression and Anxiety Treatment in the Mat-Su Valley
sub: If new motherhood feels dark, anxious, or numb, you are not a bad mom. You are unwell, it is common, and it is very treatable.
bodyHtml:
Home / Services / Postpartum Depression and Anxiety Treatment in the Mat-Su Valley

PHOTO PLACEHOLDER, add a warm, on-brand image for this page

If becoming a mother has felt more like drowning than glowing, please hear this clearly. You are not failing, and you are not a bad mother. You may be experiencing postpartum depression or anxiety, which affects a large share of new moms, is not your fault, and gets better with the right help. We support new mothers across the Mat-Su Valley.

More than the baby blues

A weepy, overwhelmed couple of weeks after birth is common and usually passes. When low mood, anxiety, or numbness lasts longer than two weeks and starts to color everything, it has likely become something that deserves real support. That is treatable, and reaching out is a sign of strength, not weakness.

What postpartum struggles can look like

  • Persistent sadness, emptiness, or crying, or feeling numb and disconnected from your baby.
  • Constant worry, racing thoughts, or dread that something bad will happen.
  • Scary intrusive thoughts, which are a common symptom, not a sign you would act on them.
  • Exhaustion beyond normal, and feeling like a failure or a burden.

You can learn more in our articles on postpartum anxiety and depression and the identity shift of matrescence.

Why the Mat-Su can make it harder

Long Alaska winters, distance from family, and the isolation many new mothers feel here can deepen postpartum struggles. None of that means you are weak. It means you are human and depleted, and you deserve support.

Effective, compassionate help

Postpartum depression and anxiety respond very well to treatment. Therapy helps, sometimes alongside medication that can be safe while breastfeeding, which your doctor can advise on. We see new mothers in person in the Valley and by telehealth, so you can get help even on the hardest days. If you are ever in crisis, call or text 988.

What to expect at your first session

Reaching out is the hardest step, so we keep the first one simple. Your first session is an unhurried conversation to understand what brought you in and what you are hoping for. There is no pressure to tell your whole story at once. It is also your chance to see whether we are the right fit, because the relationship between you and your counselor matters more than anything else. Sessions run about fifty minutes, in person or by secure video, and we will explain confidentiality and next steps clearly. You can read more in what to expect in your first therapy session.

Common questions

How do I know if it is postpartum depression or just the baby blues?

The baby blues usually pass within two weeks. If low mood, anxiety, or numbness lasts longer and affects your daily life and your bond with your baby, it may be postpartum depression or anxiety, which deserves support.

Are scary thoughts a sign something is wrong with me?

Intrusive, distressing thoughts are a common symptom of postpartum anxiety, and they are upsetting precisely because they go against your values. Tell a professional, who can help you understand and ease them.

Can I do sessions from home with a newborn?

Yes. Getting out with a new baby is hard, so telehealth from home is often ideal. We work with you to make sessions doable during this season.

h1: Trauma Therapy and EMDR in Palmer, Alaska
sub: If the past keeps intruding on the present, you can heal. We offer EMDR and trauma informed therapy for Palmer and the Mat-Su Valley.
bodyHtml:
Home / Services / Trauma Therapy and EMDR in Palmer, Alaska

PHOTO PLACEHOLDER, add a warm, on-brand image for this page

Trauma has a way of staying present long after the danger has passed, in your sleep, your reactions, your relationships. If that is your experience, here is the hopeful truth. Trauma is highly treatable, and with the right support your nervous system can finally learn that it is safe. We offer trauma therapy and EMDR right here in Palmer and across the Mat-Su Valley.

You are not stuck for good

Many people carry trauma for years, quietly assuming this is just how they are. It is not. Whether your trauma came from one overwhelming event or from years of hard experiences, healing is possible, and it does not require you to relive every detail to get there.

What we help Palmer clients with

  • PTSD and a body that stays on high alert.
  • The adult effects of childhood trauma, including anxiety, perfectionism, and people pleasing.
  • Healing after emotional abuse and toxic relationships.
  • The weight of family secrets and generational patterns.

How EMDR helps

EMDR is one of the most researched trauma treatments, and it helps the brain reprocess stuck memories so they stop feeling like they are happening now. The work is paced and manageable, and many people find real relief. Read more in what is EMDR, and about what becomes possible after healing in post-traumatic growth.

Palmer based, Valley wide

We are based in the Mat-Su Valley, so Palmer clients can work with us in person, and we offer secure telehealth across Alaska for anyone who prefers or needs it. We go at your pace, building safety first, because that is how lasting healing happens.

What to expect at your first session

Reaching out is the hardest step, so we keep the first one simple. Your first session is an unhurried conversation to understand what brought you in and what you are hoping for. There is no pressure to tell your whole story at once. It is also your chance to see whether we are the right fit, because the relationship between you and your counselor matters more than anything else. Sessions run about fifty minutes, in person or by secure video, and we will explain confidentiality and next steps clearly. You can read more in what to expect in your first therapy session.

Common questions

Is EMDR available in Palmer?

Yes. We offer EMDR and trauma informed therapy for Palmer and the wider Mat-Su Valley, in person and by secure telehealth across Alaska.

Will trauma therapy make me relive everything?

No. Good trauma therapy, including EMDR, is paced to feel manageable and does not require reliving every detail. We build safety and grounding first, then process at a pace that works for you.

Can childhood trauma still affect me as an adult?

Very much. Early trauma often shows up later as anxiety, perfectionism, people pleasing, or difficulty trusting. The good news is that it responds well to treatment at any age.
